main_text.p: quod vertit D. Erpenius, pluviam, lege (السرى & verte νυκτοπεία Profectionem nocturnam." (inquit Author AlKamusi) est سفر عامة الليل Per-nox itineratio. Occurrit proverbium apud AlHari-rium c. 43. ubi Alshirazi in Scholiis هذا مثل يضرب في تحريض احمد علي تحمل المشقة في الامر لان من تحمل المشقة يجب بعدها راحة لان من سري في الليل فعند الصباح بلغ المنزل او قاربهSic Alzamach[?]
main_text.notes: Arabic words in the first lines are read with doubt: "السرى" and "احمد" [?]. The Greek "νυκτοπεία" is uncertain in its first letters. The marginal note is cut at its end, so its later words are not visible.
main_text.p: فيفرح بالسري Proverbium est quod usurpatur ad incitandum aliquem, ut ferat molestiam in re aliqua, quòd post illam requiem inventurus sit, quoniam qui noctu iter facit, ubi mane domum suam pervenit, vel non longè ab ea abest, lætatur se noctem in itinere consumsisse. Suadet igitur molestiam alacri animo subire quâ ad quietem via struitur. Incitat patientiâ res aggredi atque animum firmare læti exitus expectatione. Alii AlMid. & Temthal, يضرب للرجل المشقة [?] رجا الراحة Dicitur cum quis alacri animo molestiam perfert, spe quietis futuræ.
main_text.head: CENTURIA II.
main_text.p: Prov. 1. دقكّ بالمنخار حبّ الفلفل Dakkaca bel menchari habbol'pholpholi. Pungit te in naso granum piperis.] lege دقكّ بالمنحاز حبّ القلقل Dakkoca belmenhazi habba l'kelkeli, Comminuis in mortario granum {*}Alkelkel. * In aliquibus Kamusi exemplaribus legitur AlKolkol. cum Dhamma. Citatur ab Aljauhario in ق ل & in AlKamus in ق ل & ز [?]. Est autem (referente Al-Jauhario) Alkelkel اصلب ما يكون من الحبوب Omnium granorum durissimum. Male igitur à non-nullis

page.notes: Arabic and Greek-like characters are transcribed from a small, partly cut scan; the Arabic vowel marks and the inline Arabic words in the Alii line and the lexicon citations (ق ل, ز) are uncertain and marked [?] where doubtful. "Z z" is a gathering signature, placed in the foot element. The word "nullis" is set as the continuation of "non-", as printed.
